clue.text: Some people are optimistic, hoping for a cut

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the words that follow are used, so a run is taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A cheerful group hopes for a reduction in something, perhaps prices or taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals that the letters sit inside 'optimistiC HOPing', running across the join of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A chop is a downward stroke with a blade, a kind of cut.

clue.text: After a number a man gets a feeling of discomfort

indicators.note: this word sets the man's letters after the article and the number in the answer

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Someone describes a man who feels unwell after being given a number, perhaps in a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts HE (a man) behind A and C (the Roman hundred).
explanation.definitionFit: A dull continuous pain is a lasting physical discomfort.

clue.text: Move away quickly when there's a trainee in charge

indicators.note: the trainee's letter is placed inside the word for charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
L is the learner plate, marking a trainee driver

explanation.surface: Staff decide to run off when a novice is put in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in charge' looks like a phrase about who is boss; here 'in' puts L (the learner sign) inside FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To run from danger is to depart in haste.

clue.text: A composer composing in tears

indicators.note: composing means putting together afresh, so the letters of the next words are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A songwriter weeps as they work on a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: John Stainer was a Victorian English composer of church music, best known for The Crucifixion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Stainer was a nineteenth-century English organist and writer of church music.

clue.text: Conclude cross is at risk

parts.note: to end is to conclude
cross as an adjective means annoyed, angered

explanation.surface: Someone decides that a crossing, or a cross, is in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as a noun or verb; it is the adjective meaning annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A species or thing in danger of harm or extinction is threatened.

clue.text: The explorer slack? Not he! That would be quite wrong

indicators.note: something quite wrong is badly out of order, so the letters of the quoted words are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protests that calling a famous polar explorer lazy would be utterly unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest Shackleton led Antarctic expeditions; his letters come from SLACK and NOT HE rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Ernest Shackleton was an Anglo-Irish leader of Antarctic expeditions.

clue.text: This may well be assumed by the retiring girl

definitions.text: This may well be assumed by the retiring girl

parts.words: This may well be assumed by the retiring girl
parts.note: assumed means put on, as clothing, and retiring means going to bed rather than shy, so this is what a girl wears for sleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' suggests a shy girl and 'assumed' an attitude she takes on; she is going to bed and putting on a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A long loose garment worn in bed is what a woman or girl puts on at bedtime.

clue.text: Impotent heel

definitions.meaning: unable, powerless: something one cannot do
to heel over is to tilt or lean to one side

explanation.walkthrough: Read as CAN'T, the first sense is 'unable'; the second is the verb meaning to lean over, as a ship does.
explanation.definitionFit: One who is powerless is unable to act, and a ship that heels tilts or slants.

clue.text: Craft setting fish record

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
an entry is an item set down in a record or ledger

explanation.surface: A trade involves putting a fish into the record books.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodworking is a skilled trade, a craft.

clue.text: Going in front before giving up

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
ceding means surrendering or giving up

explanation.surface: Someone walks ahead before surrendering.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that comes earlier in order or position goes before the rest.

clue.text: Start consuming very large lettuce

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, taken from consuming

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: Someone begins eating an enormous salad leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a clothing-size label; cos is a long-leafed lettuce, also called romaine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos is a variety of crisp, long-leaved salad plant, also called romaine.

clue.text: Sat on a horse, we hear, this way

indicators.note: this tells the solver to go by sound, so the word for riding is replaced by one said the same

parts.note: rode means sat on and rode a horse

explanation.surface: Someone rode along this route on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: A street or route is a way from one place to another.

clue.text: Plant for spring

definitions.meaning: a climbing plant whose cones flavour beer
to spring on one foot is to leap or jump

explanation.definitionFit: The climbing vine used in brewing shares its name with a short jump.

clue.text: Diversion caused by new mate's menu

indicators.note: new makes the letters of the following words into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the letters of the word as printed, its S included

explanation.surface: A friend's restaurant menu provides some fun.
explanation.definitionFit: An entertainment or pastime is a diversion from routine.

clue.text: A lofty paper produced on every occasion

parts.note: something lofty is high, tall
The Times is a British national newspaper

explanation.surface: A grand newspaper appears again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: THE TIMES is a London daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Always, without exception, is a synonym for on every occasion.

clue.text: Due to turn-around, given no instruction

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the letters of the preceding words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone untaught because of an about-face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn-around' reads as one word, but TURN belongs to the fodder DUE TO TURN and 'around' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untaught has had no teaching or tuition.

clue.text: Left after breakfast maybe, a woman will get gripped by urges

indicators.note: the woman's letters are held inside the word for urges

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
she'll is the short form of she will, a woman will

explanation.surface: A woman feels driven by strong impulses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'urges' looks like a noun; it is the verb, as in egging someone on, and 'a woman will' contracts to one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The broken casings are what remain on the plate after a boiled-egg meal.

clue.text: Returning servicemen get leave in consequence

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the soldiers' abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British army servicemen
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Soldiers coming home are granted leave as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' looks like military leave; it is the verb GO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for therefore means as a consequence.

clue.text: Carry on about a teetotaller's power

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for carry on goes round the other letters

parts.note: to wage war is to carry it on
TT is short for teetotal, a teetotaller

explanation.surface: Keep going on about the strength of a non-drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry on' is not a plea to continue but the verb used of war: one wages it. TT is the usual crossword shorthand for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount of electrical energy used, measured in watts, is a measure of power.

clue.text: Post Office with back door

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A Post Office building has a rear entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a small back or side gate or door, especially in a castle wall.

clue.text: One holding on — it appears to be a poisonous plant

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the word for one surrounds the other letters

parts.note: an ace is the one in cards or dice

explanation.surface: Someone clinging on reveals a dangerous plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The ace is the card or die face worth one. The plant is also called monkshood or wolfsbane.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, also called monkshood or wolfsbane, is a highly toxic flowering plant.

clue.text: It's not very exciting but it's home

definitions.meaning: an apartment, a home on one floor of a building

explanation.definitionFit: Something dull is lifeless, and a set of rooms on one floor is an apartment.

clue.text: Common, cheeky, and wild

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of the preceding words run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is described as vulgar, impudent and unruly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheeky' and 'wild' look like more items in the list; with 'and' they are the anagram and its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Trite and overused, as a stale phrase is, means commonplace.

clue.text: An article on Queen Eliza a beth's age

indicators.note: in this clue on means placed after, so the article follows the queen

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the cipher of Queen Elizabeth
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone describes a piece about the age of Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Latin for Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch or period of history is an age.

clue.text: Individual in fashion — elegant too

indicators.note: the answer is found in the letters of the words that follow, across the dash

explanation.surface: Someone is stylish and also refined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals that the answer sits within 'fashiON — Elegant'.
explanation.definitionFit: A single person or thing is a unit, one.

clue.text: Support by housing one

indicators.note: housing means containing, so the word for by holds the other letter

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something holds one up by giving it a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar supporting a bridge or arch is a support.

clue.text: Guides will take English money as well as German

parts.note: L stands for the pound sterling, English money
and means as well as
marks were the money of Germany before the euro

explanation.surface: Tour guides accept both pounds and German currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' borrows 'money' from earlier: MARKS were German currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Prominent features that help travellers find their way serve as guides.

clue.text: Only French mother

definitions.meaning: the word a child in France uses formally for a female parent

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective meaning just or nothing more than is spelt like the French word for a female parent.

clue.text: Walk with no particular purpose? That sounds capital!

indicators.note: the solver hears the capital's name, which is said the same as the answer

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Wandering aimlessly sounds a marvellous idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital!' looks like an exclamation of delight; it is the city of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander is to move about without aim.

clue.text: Poles turning reverential for a bit

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles

indicators.note: turning means turned round, so the abbreviation for reverential is read backwards

parts.note: pi is a short form of pious, reverential

explanation.surface: People from Poland become devout for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland; it is the compass poles S and N. 'turning' makes IP of PI (pious).
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is a small piece cut off, a scrap.

clue.text: An element of initiative

definitions.meaning: a heavy grey metallic chemical element, symbol Pb
taking the ... means taking the initiative

explanation.definitionFit: The soft heavy metal Pb is a chemical element, and the front position in action shows initiative.

clue.text: Australian agitation for a jollification

indicators.note: agitation stirs things up, so the letters of the word before it are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: An Australian gets worked up about a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Saturnalia was the Roman midwinter festival; the word now means any wild revelry.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnalia, from the Roman feast, is a period of unrestrained revelry or merrymaking.
